tasks.short: Record materials processed and operational data

steps.what: Measure or read the amount of materials processed and identify the production batch
Copy production and operational data into the required record fields
Check and record the final production and operational entry

tasks.design: Configure a native entry form in {OPS_SYSTEM} so the worker captures the observation once and the required log fields are populated from that entry. The worker still measures or reads the processed amount, checks its meaning and confirms the final record.
tasks.previous_blocker: An observed quantity may be copied into a second tally or log form.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse captured batch and quantity fields without interpreting the physical operation.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether a counter represents input, processed output or rejected material.
tasks.human_edge: The worker sees the operation and recognises a misleading quantity or wrong batch.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate copying; physical observation and record responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Agree how processed quantity and rejects are recorded

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native production forms can reuse verified observation fields. The digest's warehouse capability does not establish machine-feeder capture coverage or a local time saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the worker's production record, excluding feeding, processing, moving material and supervisor analysis. Existing counter runtime is not human effort.

In s1 the machine feeder produces and captures timestamp, machine ID, batch ID, material ID, processed quantity, unit, reading source and any reject or correction note. All observation, identification and first-entry time remains in the 60% share; no free structured processed-quantity flag is assumed.

Existing counters or scales provide readings only where already installed. The worker checks whether the reading actually measures processed output. Missing identifiers, disputed units or unsuitable readings return to manual counting and recording; no new sensor or automatic physical measurement is presumed.

The production records owner verifies form mappings and quantity definitions, with 3 other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours counted for upkeep. Six additional focal hours cover changed forms, correction checks and extra exceptions.

Test native form reuse before custom code. If the current process already records once, or paper is required in addition, retain it with zero new saving. No extra supervisor or operator capture work is transferred without counting it.
unknowns: Current duplicate entry and acceptance of electronic logs
Meaning and reliability of existing counters or scale readings
research_questions: Is there genuinely a second transcription after initial observation capture?
Can the native form distinguish processed output from input and rejects without new worker effort?

already_counted.description: Measurement, batch identification and structured first capture

incremental.description: Form changes, correction checks and additional exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact log entry, batch, material, machine, timestamp, quantity, unit and observation source checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+15=75; gross 25%, net 19% after 6 focal upkeep. Range covers existing single-entry records with no gain through 14 points of duplicate copying removed minus 6 upkeep. All observation and first capture remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The worker captures once and verifies the resulting record while physical material handling stays unchanged.
reach: Coordinate quantity definitions with the production supervisor.
role.ambitious_version: Traceable operational entries with measured savings only where duplicate transcription exists.
